answer: A reef survey crew maps one patch of coral each epoch. The agent drops an anchor chain into a karst sinkhole at a marked coordinate and counts links to the limestone floor, then a second boat drops its own chain into the same sinkhole and both readings must match within one link. A copied reading fails because the floor slopes and the tide shifts the chain, so only a live drop in that hour gives the true count. A thousand fake surveyors would need a thousand boats over the reef, a thousand anchor chains, and a thousand readings matched within one link.
